messages:
nina: FYI we're seeing a large drop in KV cache hit rate for prefix keys starting ~10:22 UTC. Backend error rate and p99 latency climbing. Investigating.
ben: Pulled the metric: promql `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[5m]))` — hit_rate ~1.2% for prefix namespace 'org:' (normally ~70-80%).
sam: I can repro. Tokenizer change from yesterday is injecting org ids into prefix keys (namespace collision). Local diff shows keys changed: `pref_key=Hello` -> `pref_key=org_42:Hello`.
liz: That would explain the miss wave. Most requests are now cache-misses and falling back to the full model path. We're seeing kernel fallback to the slower cuBLAS->fallback execution and batching windows grow.
ben: Quick profile: recent flame shows kernel latency jump `45ms -> 120ms` per request on the fallback path; KV proxy CPU at 92% and queueing.
sam: I'm toggling the new normalization feature off in canary:
```
redwoodctl runtime config set tokenizer.inject_org_prefix=false --env=canary
```
Rolling to 10%.
deploy-bot: deployment nina/token-prefix-toggle started by sam at 2026-03-18T10:35:10Z — rollout 10%.
ops-bot: Suggested mitigations: 1) rate-limit fallback path (protect backends), 2) prewarm cache with top-K prefixes for affected orgs, 3) temporarily reject or truncate namespace tokens to avoid explosion.
nina: Applying fallback throttle now:
```
redwoodctl policy set fallback_throttle rate=200rps burst=500 --scope=global
```
Applying.
ben: Also kicking off a quick prewarm job: bulk `kv.put` for top 10k prefixes for the high-traffic orgs. Script pushed to staging.
sam: After rollback toggle + throttling in canary, hit_rate jumped to ~68% within 90s and backend CPU dropped ~40%. Behavior looks healthy so far.
liz: Next steps: keep tokenizer change disabled, add compatibility/unit tests for key normalization, add perf alert on `kv_cache_hit_rate < 30% for 2m`, and add circuit-breaker on KV proxy CPU > 80%.
nina: I'll open the postmortem and link deployment artifacts. cc @oncall — thanks for the quick responses. :thumbsup:
ben: Summary: root cause = namespace injection into prefix keys (tokenizer change); impact = cache miss wave -> backend overload -> kernel fallback -> p99 regressions; mitigations = feature flag rollback, fallback throttling, cache prewarm.
sam: I'll attach PromQL queries and flamegraphs to the postmortem (traces + profiles).
nina: End of thread — will close after postmortem linked. Thanks all :heart:
